rows: reads the step-64 telling after the junction
caption: 1000 episodes per seed and run, same episodes in all three runs (same seed). Junction step = median episode step at which the agent reaches the junction, range over seeds. The last three rows are the rerun with a random telling phase (first telling at a uniform step 0–63, then every 64; 15 runs, Nov 15–16).
bullets: At L = 32 the step-64 telling lands at the decision. Agents reach the junction 50–79 steps into the episode, so the second telling arrives just before the junction (slower LSTM seeds) or just after it, before a room is entered (FS16). "Every 64" is in practice "told at the start and again at the decision".
FS16's 4/5 at every 64 is not body memory: blinded from the bend it falls to chance on every seed. Its "every 16" success also needs the tellings inside the corridor.
The LSTM remembers at every 4 and 16 (blinding changes nothing), but at every 64 only 2 of 5 seeds do; the other 3 wait for the late telling.
The MLP's "every 4" success needs the tellings in the corridor (blinded: chance). Steering bridges the 3 blank steps between tellings, not the corridor.

Rerun with a random telling phase (15 runs): the last telling before the junction is now 0–63 steps old (median 24–32). The LSTM solves 5/5 and swapping its recurrent state flips the choice (hidden_other 0.01–0.02), so it remembers. The MLP stays at chance; only a telling 0–3 steps old lifts it a little (0.55–0.68 on 4 seeds).

FS16 now solves 5/5 by body memory: success doesn't change when blinded from the bend and is 0.99–1.00 even when the last telling is 32–63 steps old, beyond its 16 frames; the cue is decodable from its pose at the junction at 0.96–1.00. With the late telling gone, training found the body-memory strategy that FS16 never found when never told (0/5) or with the fixed phase.
